title: Book One · Chapter 39: The Hard Word
story:
Ronan opens his reading book. He does not like one word on this page. It comes near the bottom of a page about a market. He reads down the page. At that word, he jumps to the next one.

At home, Mum sometimes notices. At school, he says the next word quickly. He does not want Miss Wu to notice.

Leo hears it on Tuesday.

“You missed one.”

“I know the story.”

“We're reading the words.”

Ronan pushes the book a little away. Leo reads the whole line. He does not stop at any word. It sounds easy in his voice.

“You always want to win,” Ronan says.

Leo shuts his book. “I was telling you.”

For the rest of the pair work, they use their own books. Ronan holds his finger over the difficult word. It doesn't become easier under his finger.

Miss Wu comes past with a pile of papers. She asks him to read the line. He misses the word again. This time she stops him.

“Do you know that one?”

He shakes his head.

She sits beside him for a short moment. She says the word in two parts. Ronan says each part after her. Then he puts them together. “A person buys something at the market,” Miss Wu says. “That person is a customer.” Mum uses that word at home.

“Oh,” he says. “That word.”

“You know this word from home. These letters spell that word. You can learn to read it now.”

She asks him to read the line again. He reads it slowly. This time, he does not miss a word.

At break, Leo is drawing a station platform. He put too many windows in the train.

“Look at these doors,” he tells another boy. “My dad told me about them. They are different on some trains.”

Ronan waits nearby. Leo doesn't look up immediately. Ronan stands beside the desk. He can speak or go away. He decides to speak.

“It was customer,” he says.

Leo turns. “I know.”

“Mum says the word at home. I know it from her voice. But I could not read the letters.”

Leo considers this. Then he nods. “That happens to me with long names.”

Leo takes out an old ticket paper. His father brought it home. There is a street name on it. Leo shows that name to Ronan. Neither boy can read the whole thing. The little letters run into each other. Neither boy can separate them.

The name is new to both boys. They put it away for now. Miss Wu is calling them back to the lesson.

After school, Ronan takes his market page to Mr Qiu's stall. Mum needs a small packet of needles, and Mr Qiu stocks a few beside the thread. A woman is buying a pencil. Ronan points to her.

“Customer,” he says quietly.

“Correct,” Mr Qiu says. “And this customer wants a red pencil. I am holding a blue one. I need to change it!”

He changes pencils and finishes the sale. The woman smiles at Ronan. Then she leaves.

Mum picks up a needle packet. “Can you read this word?” she asks Ronan. He reads the large word at the top but stops at a smaller one below it.

“I do not know this one,” he says. He points to it.

Mr Qiu reads it for him. The word and number go together. They tell Mum the number of needles. She needs to check that number first. Ronan finds it on each packet. One packet has more needles. Mum chooses that one. Ronan keeps his finger beside the number. Mum looks at it and nods.

At home, Ronan reads the page to Dad. He goes slowly through the whole line. Dad doesn't clap. “Is there a bun shop at this market?” Dad asks. “I am hungry.”

Ronan turns the page to check. There is one. A man stands beside the shop. He has a bag in his hand.

“A customer,” Ronan reads. His finger stays below the word this time. Then he reads the next line. This time he says every word. Dad listens. He can follow the story now.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：customer＝顾客；letters＝字母；number＝数字；needles＝针。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 为什么总是跳过那个词？
2. Leo 和 Miss Wu 各自给了他什么不同的帮助？
